name: Captify
oneLine: Captioning smart glasses for deaf and hard of hearing people that show live captions, translations and sound alerts in the lenses, run by the free Captify Glass app on iPhone or Android.

platforms.text: Captify glasses + iPhone or Android app
platforms.detail: Captions show in Captify's own glasses (Captify Pro or Captify Light), run by the free Captify Glass app on an iPhone or Android phone. The App Store lists the app for iPhone only, and Captify says a phone is required for captioning.

deviceRequirements.detail: Captify lists iOS 16 or later and Android 12 or later. The phone has to stay within Bluetooth range of the glasses (about 10 m / 30 feet), because speech is turned into text on the phone.

roomCaptions.text: Yes, shown in the glasses' lenses
roomCaptions.detail: The glasses' two directional microphones, or the phone's microphone, pick up speech nearby, and the captions appear in the lenses, in your line of sight. Captify doesn't say whether the app can caption on the phone screen without the glasses.

groupConversations.text: Small groups; not several people at once
groupConversations.detail: Captify lists family gatherings and small groups among the places Captify Pro works best, and several people speaking at once, or very loud and crowded places, as not ideal. The glasses' microphones focus on the person in front of you; for a speaker further away you can switch to the phone's microphone.

languages.detail: Captify lists 80+ languages and regional variants for Captify Pro and Captify Light, with more coming soon. Its subscription page counts 30+ languages for free offline captions. The older Captify Myvu supports 13 languages.

offline.detail: Captify says no internet is needed: captions can run on an offline model, and the free plan has unlimited offline captions in 30+ languages. An online model can be chosen in Settings. A help article says real-time translation needs internet, while the subscription page lists free offline translation in 20+ languages.

speakerLabels.detail: The App Store release notes added speaker labelling in February 2026, and Captify's comparison page lists speaker labeling for Captify Pro. The subscription page lists speaker differentiation as part of the Premium plan, which it marks Coming Soon.

translation.text: Yes, live, in the glasses; 80+ languages
translation.detail: Translated captions show in the glasses. Captify's product pages say 80+ languages, a help article (August 2026) says over 40, and says translation needs internet; the subscription page lists free offline translations in 20+ languages. A two-way mode is not described.

saveTranscripts.text: Yes, in the app; cloud sync is Premium
saveTranscripts.detail: Transcripts are saved on the app's home screen after each session, sorted into captions and translations. Cloud backup and sync across devices is listed for the Premium plan, marked Coming Soon. Keeping the audio is not described.

export.detail: The App Store release notes for version 1.0.9 (October 2025) mention fixing the Save to PDF function. Other ways to share a transcript are not described.

fileUpload.detail: Transcribing an uploaded audio or video file is not described on Captify's pages.

summaries.detail: The App Store release notes added conversation summaries in January 2026. The subscription page lists AI summaries, and Ask AI to search your saved conversations, under the Premium plan, marked Coming Soon.

customWords.detail: Custom keywords came with app version 1.3.5 (September 2026), online only. The subscription page lists custom word recognition for names and jargon under the Premium plan, marked Coming Soon.

display.detail: Captify Pro has three font sizes (Regular, Large, Extra-Large), captions that can move to the top, bottom or sides of your view, adjustable brightness and a high-contrast monochrome display. One of its two displays can be turned off. Captify Light has a single-eye display.

soundAlerts.text: Yes, 300+ sounds, on the free plan
soundAlerts.detail: Non-speech sounds such as doorbells, sirens, laughter, applause, alarms and music are shown in the glasses. The subscription page counts 300+ sounds on the free Standard plan; the Captify Light page says 500+.

phoneCalls.detail: Captify's comparison page lists phone call transcription among Captify Pro's AI features. No other Captify page explains how it works.

videoCalls.detail: Captioning video calls is not described on Captify's pages.

mediaOnDevice.detail: Captioning audio or video playing on the phone is not described.

humanCaptioners.detail: No human captioners are described; captions come from speech recognition.

privacy.text: On the phone, offline or online
privacy.detail: Captify says speech is turned into text on the phone, with Microsoft's speech recognition model, and you choose an offline or an online model. Its privacy policy (March 2025) does not mention audio; the App Store privacy label lists audio data linked to you, and Google Play says no data is shared with third parties.

account.detail: Captify's setup guide for Captify Myvu says to sign in to the app with your phone number and a verification code. The App Store privacy label lists name, email address and user ID.

availability.text: Glasses ship worldwide; free US shipping
availability.detail: Captify ships anywhere in the world (190+ countries, says the Captify Pro page), free within the continental US; other buyers pay shipping and any import duties. The app is in English.

freePlan.detail: The app is free with no in-app purchases on the US App Store. Captify's $0 Standard plan includes unlimited offline captions (30+ languages), offline translation (20+ languages), sound alerts and note-taking. You need Captify glasses, which you buy.

price.text: Pro US$849, Light US$499; Premium US$15/mo (soon)
price.detail: Captify's US store, October 2026: Captify Pro US$849 and Captify Light US$499 at regular price (on sale for US$699 and US$399 in late October 2026); new prescription lenses start at US$99. A Premium plan at US$15 a month is announced as Coming Soon; the app is free on the US App Store, with no in-app purchases.

accessibilityFunding.text: US: FSA/HSA cards; insurance may reimburse
accessibilityFunding.detail: Captify takes FSA and HSA cards at checkout, and vision insurance plans that cover out-of-network glasses may pay you back. No government programme is named.

strengths.text: Captions appear in the glasses' lenses, in your line of sight, so you can keep looking at the person speaking.
The free Standard plan includes unlimited offline captions in 30+ languages, with no internet needed.
It shows non-speech sounds such as doorbells, sirens, laughter and applause, on the free plan.
The glasses come with single vision, reading or progressive prescription lenses, and US buyers can pay with FSA or HSA cards.

Captify Pro gives 3 to 4 hours of continuous captioning with both displays on, and up to 6 hours with one.

Speaker differentiation, summaries, custom words and cloud sync are listed for a Premium plan marked Coming Soon.

notes: Different app, same name: 'Captify: Live Caption Deaf+HoH' (App Store id 6449643108, bundle com.inquiryhealth.captify, seller Inquiry Health LLC, version 1.0 released 2 June 2023, never updated) is not by Captify Inc.: different seller, different bundle id, no link to it on captify.glass, and Captify's help centre tells buyers to make sure the app is developed by Captify. It is left out of every fact. Company names differ by page: App Store seller 'Captify Incorporated', Google Play developer 'Captify Inc.' with a Houston, Texas address, privacy policy and terms 'Captify Glass, Inc.', site footer 'Captify Inc.'; the FAQ says the team is based in San Francisco. Products: Captify Pro (two displays) and Captify Light (the Light page says 'Single-eye display' and 'Monocular diffractive waveguide' but also 'Captions appear in both lenses'); the older Captify Myvu is still covered by the FAQ and help centre but not sold on the product menu. The Light page is not described as a rename of Myvu (it compares itself to Myvu). Premium: the subscription page and the Captify Pro page mark Captify Premium (US$15/month) 'Coming Soon', but the FAQ says 'Upgrade to the optional $15/mo premium subscription' without that label; the US App Store lists no in-app purchases (checked in the page data), so the cells treat Premium as announced, not on sale. Several Premium features (speaker labelling Feb 2026, conversation summary Jan 2026, custom keywords Sep 2026) are already in the app's release notes; whether they will need Premium is unclear. Translation: help article (Aug 2026) says real-time translation needs internet and supports over 40 languages; product pages say 80+; subscription page lists free offline translation in 20+ languages; app version 1.3.5 (Sep 2026) added offline translation for non-English languages. Language counts also differ: App Store description 'over a dozen', release notes '40+' (Sep 2025), product pages and FAQ '80+', subscription page '30+' for offline captions; the FAQ and product page differ slightly on which languages are 'coming soon'. Sound count: subscription page 300+, Light page 500+. Battery: Pro page 4 hours continuous and 20 hours standby; help article 3-4 hours binocular, up to 6 hours monocular, 48-hour standby; comparison page 4 hours / 6+ hours. Trial: 14 days on the homepage, FAQ and return policy, 15 days on the Light page. Shipping time: FAQ 1-2 weeks; an older help article says about 4 weeks. Prices were read in USD with a US localisation cookie (the site shows euros from Europe); the Pro US$699 price is a Halloween sale (regular US$849); lens add-on prices on the product page are set in a lens picker that was not read, so only the help centre's 'starting at $99' for new prescription lenses is used. Whether the app captions on the phone screen without glasses is not stated. The privacy policy (March 2025) does not cover audio or AI training; Captify's FAQ names Microsoft as its speech model. The captify.glass site rate-limited automated requests (HTTP 429), so pages were downloaded slowly by script; the help centre (help.captify.glass) renders client-side and its article URLs were taken from its own route code. No Captify page states accessibility features beyond captions, and no ratings, review counts or user counts are used.
